function_calls in gemini.rs numbers ids gemini-call-0.. from zero on every response, so a multi-round tool conversation repeats the same ids across rounds; if the transcript is later replayed to a provider that requires unique tool-use ids (for example a fallback to Anthropic mid-loop) or a loop keys results by id, the rounds collide.

stop_reason maps any finishReason other than STOP/MAX_TOKENS to its lowercase name, so MALFORMED_FUNCTION_CALL yields a response with no tool_calls that execution-core (which branches on tool_calls.is_empty()) reads as a final answer; map it to a typed refusal before S8.

routing_diff takes its price and ZDR-attestation facts as injected RouteFacts, and inference-core has no production source for either; the diff is therefore not reachable at runtime yet, and the unpriced-model and ZDR-change flags are untested against real price rows.
No route can load an unpromoted candidate's config into a non-ZDR test inference-core, so the live leg in eval-routing-candidate.sh cannot run end to end; the script was never executed.

The unpriced-model check treats the tool fallback ladder and side-task role candidates as routed models, not only the mode table and cheap fallback; the owner should confirm that reading.

The gate fails closed and the switch defaults off, so this is safe; do not flip the switch before this lands.

routing_diff is reachable only from tests: nothing at runtime calls diff(), and inference-core has no production source for RouteFacts (price rows, ZDR attestation), so the unpriced-model and ZDR-route flags have no real data behind them yet.

Audit trail: promote_candidate writes decided_by = the promoter over the reviewer's decided_by set in record_candidate_evaluation. The candidate row then loses who accepted the diff and the waiver, which is the record S10 exists to keep. A separate reviewed_by/promoted_by column, or not overwriting the field, would keep both.

proposed_by, decided_by and updated_by are taken from the request body, not from the verified caller identity, so an admin or service caller can record any name in the audit trail. updated_by already worked this way before this slice.

ProposeCandidate and PromoteCandidate store and promote config_json after a JSON-parse check only. A direct gRPC caller with admin scope can therefore make a config live that inference-core's serde or role validation would refuse; SetPolicy has the same gap today.

eval-routing-candidate.sh requires ROUTING_EVAL_ORG_ID but never passes it to the eval-lab run. The ZDR refusal checks only a `zdr` claim in the bearer, so nothing ties the live leg to the named non-ZDR test org.

No test covers two concurrent promotes, or a promote racing set_policy. By reading the code, promoting the same candidate twice makes the second call answer FAILED_PRECONDITION ('candidate is promoted'), not the ABORTED that the DoD expects.
candidate_rpcs_need_admin_scope asserts the member denial for propose and list only. The admin check on record_candidate_evaluation and promote_candidate is not tested individually.
